# Pipeline (CI/CD, ETL)

**Use when:** you need the ordered stages of a build/release or data pipeline, with gates and artifacts.

## Purpose
A stage-by-stage view of an automated pipeline: CI/CD (commit -> build -> test ->
deploy) or ETL/ELT jobs. It answers "what happens, in what order, what gates
promotion, and what is produced?" for engineers and release managers.

## Spec settings
- `"type": "pipeline"`, `"layout": "flowchart-lr"` (time runs left to right).
- Theme `professional`.

## Node kinds
| Kind | Use for |
|---|---|
| `start` / `end` | Trigger (`Push to Main`, `Nightly 02:00`) and completion. |
| `build`, `test`, `deploy`, `process` | A stage or job: `Build Image`, `Unit Tests`, `Deploy Staging`. |
| `decision` | A gate: `Tests Pass?`, `Approved?` - with labeled branches. |
| `manual` | A human approval step. |
| `registry`, `artifact`, `storage`, `document` | Artifacts and outputs: image registry, package feed, report. |
| `external` | External tools invoked (scanner, ticketing). |

Stage labels are short verbs/nouns (`Build`, `Scan Image`); the tool goes in
`technology` (`GitHub Actions`, `Trivy`, `Argo CD`).

## Groups
- `environment` groups for promotion targets (Dev, Staging, Prod), or `generic`
  groups for pipeline phases (CI, CD).
- Keep it flat; one level is enough.

## Edges
- Sequence edges unlabeled; gate branches labeled (`pass`/`fail`, `approved`).
- `dashed` for artifact publish/consume edges (to registries), so the main sequence
  reads as solid.
- Failure paths go to an `end` (`Build Failed`) or a notification, not back to start.

## Checklist
- [ ] Trigger on the left, final state on the right
- [ ] Every gate is a decision with labeled branches
- [ ] Artifacts shown where they are produced and consumed
- [ ] Environments as groups, promotion order left to right
- [ ] Tools in `technology`, not in labels

## Common mistakes
- One giant box per tool instead of per stage.
- Gates hidden inside a stage label (`Test and Approve`).
- Missing failure path.
- Parallel jobs drawn in sequence; fan out from one stage and join at the next.

## Example
```json
{
  "title": "Orders API Delivery Pipeline",
  "subtitle": "GitHub Actions + Argo CD - Oct 2026",
  "type": "pipeline",
  "layout": "flowchart-lr",
  "nodes": [
    {"id": "push", "label": "Push to Main", "kind": "start"},
    {"id": "build", "label": "Build Image", "kind": "build", "technology": "Docker"},
    {"id": "test", "label": "Unit Tests", "kind": "test", "technology": "pytest"},
    {"id": "scan", "label": "Security Scan", "kind": "test", "technology": "Trivy"},
    {"id": "gate", "label": "Checks Pass?", "kind": "decision"},
    {"id": "registry", "label": "Container Registry", "kind": "registry"},
    {"id": "deploy", "label": "Deploy Staging", "kind": "deploy", "technology": "Argo CD"},
    {"id": "failed", "label": "Build Failed", "kind": "end"},
    {"id": "done", "label": "Ready for Prod", "kind": "end"}
  ],
  "edges": [
    {"source": "push", "target": "build"},
    {"source": "build", "target": "test"},
    {"source": "build", "target": "scan"},
    {"source": "test", "target": "gate"},
    {"source": "scan", "target": "gate"},
    {"source": "gate", "target": "registry", "label": "pass", "style": "dashed"},
    {"source": "gate", "target": "failed", "label": "fail"},
    {"source": "registry", "target": "deploy", "label": "image", "style": "dashed"},
    {"source": "deploy", "target": "done"}
  ]
}
```
